(Capacity: 12,508) |champion = |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2023–24 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Pittsburgh]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Panthers were led by sixth-year head coach [[Jeff Capel III|Jeff Capel]] and played their home games at the [[Petersen Events Center]] in [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Panthers won their first four games of the season before losing the opening game of their preseason tournament, the [[NIT Season Tip-Off]], to [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. They won the third place game against [[2023–24 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|Oregon State]]. They would then go on to lose their next two games, the first to [[2023–24 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] and their ACC season opener against [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]]. They then rebounded to win their next four games, including a [[Backyard Brawl|rivalry]] game against [[2023–24 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]]. The Panthers had a record of 9–2 against non-conference opponents. The Panthers lost four of their next five ACC games including to eighth-ranked [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and eleventh-ranked [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. Pittsburgh began a streak of winning seven of their next eight with a win over seventh-ranked Duke. The only loss during the stretch came at [[2023–24 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]] while they won against [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] and twenty first-ranked [[2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. They finished the season by winning four of their last six games, with losses coming again to Clemson and to [[2023–24 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]]. They defeated NC State on the final day of the season. The Panthers finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 22–11 and 12–8 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a fourth place. As the fourth seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] they received a bye into the Quarterfinals where they defeated Wake Forest. They faced North Carolina in the Semifinals where they were defeated 65–72. They were not invited to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and they were eligible to participate in the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|NIT Tournament]], but they opted not to participate.{{cite web |last1=Behanna|first1=Garett|title=Pitt declines NIT invite after missing out on NCAA tournament bid|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/pitt-mens-basketball-denied-ncaa-tournament-bid/|website=cbsnews.com|publisher=[[KDKA-TV]]|access-date=April 8, 2024|date=March 17, 2024}} ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Panthers]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 24–12, 14–6 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for third place. This season marked a surprise turnaround from previous seasons; at one point, the Panthers were ranked No. 25 in the nation, their first appearance in the top-25 rankings in seven years. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2022–23 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] before losing to [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], the Panthers' first invitation since [[2015–16 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|2016]]. As a No. 11 seed in the Midwest region, they defeated [[2022–23 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] in the First Four. They upset [[2022–23 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] in the first round before losing to [[2022–23 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] in the second round.
